newsitem.title: ITALY: Milan shares slide to lower close as lira tumbles.
newsitem.headline: Milan shares slide to lower close as lira tumbles.

text.p: Italian shares slumped to a lower close on Tuesday pressured by the lower lira and domestic bonds, while Wall Street and most European bourses traded lower.
"The market attempted to hold its ground early, but with most other domestic and international markets heading lower there was little support," said one share trader.
Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM ) was one stock to stand out, gaining against the trend, after an upbeat analysts meeting Monday in Milan and a further meeting in London this afternoon.
The all-share Mibtel ended 1.21 percent at 11,551 and the blue chip MIB30 index was down 1.24 percent at 17,058.

Shares in TIM also gained from switching out of other telecom stocks such as STET and Telecom Italia. TIM ended up 6.79 percent at 4,435 lire, while STET was off 3.46 percent at 7,205 lire and Telecom Italia down 2.21 percent at 4,080 lire.
Financial holding group Gemina was suspended limit up for much of the day, and ended the trading day up some 9.36 percent at 573.4 lire.

Among banking shares, Ambroveneto ended off 0.3 percent at 3,990 lire after its chairman Giovanni Bazoli told a news conference on Tuesday it will make a capital issue of "major dimensions" by the end of this year.
Banca Commerciale Italiana ended off 3.81 percent at 3,129 lire after reporting largely in line 1996 consolidated results late Monday.
Dealers pointed out that like the bond market, stock market sentiment was cautious with worries over EMU delays and mini budget problems effecting all Italian financial markets.
A temporary suspension to derivative trading on the Milan bourse contributed to a quiet start to share trading, with trading on the FIB30 contract temporarily suspended.
